focal_claim_text: Online commerce can extract spending from local economies via platform concentration and wealth leakage.

e_commerce_share_of_retail.note: Census retail e-commerce share — scale fact only

local_retail_displacement.note: Labor-market reallocation under Amazon Tax shocks — not wealth leakage

sales_tax_sourcing_destination_marketpla.note: Wayfair / destination-based collection — kills pre-Wayfair tax myths

consumer_welfare_effects.note: Material consumer surplus; denser/higher-income counties gain more in U.S. Visa study

rural_accessibility_benefits.note: U.S. Dolfen et al. find denser counties gain more — complicates simple rural-access benefit story for U.S.; China RCT literature not transferred

local_economic_leakage.note: Operational definition + RIMS margin discipline; measurement not complete

delivery_logistics_employment.note: Transport/warehousing complementary employment moves with e-commerce tax regime

primary_failure_modes: causal inference — 'can extract via platform concentration' untested in registered corpus
consumer_substitution — ignored consumer surplus contrary evidence
not_primary_failure: tax treatment alone (Wayfair updates tax myth, not leakage)
cc_claim_016_diagnosis.do_not_rescue_by_keyword: Finding a source that uses the word 'leakage' without an operational measure does not repair fit.

arkansas_applicability: National Census share does not equal Arkansas local leakage; need state retail/fiscal modules.
current_confidence: High for e-commerce retail share; Moderate for labor-market adjustment literature; Very Low for wealth-leakage mechanism.

claim_016_verdict_after_research.rationale: Scale + local labor adjustment + consumer surplus improve domain coverage, but current wording still asserts extraction/leakage via platform concentration without measurement. Disposition remains REWRITE REQUIRED pending Steve approval of proposed wording.
